# Command-line reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/cli_reference.py from `faris --help`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every `faris` command with its help text, which lists every option. The examples are command lines from the
rest of this handbook; [Command line](cli.md) explains how the commands fit together.

79 of 83 commands have an example in the handbook; these have none yet: `faris materials show`, `faris evidence run`, `faris evidence stage`, `faris cache unpin`.

## faris

```text
Fusion Analysis and Reactor Integration Simulator

Usage: faris [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  history      Calculate or validate the shared Rust operating-history ledger
  activation   Activation inventory, decay heat and decay-photon source of zones through ACTINV
  maintenance  Compute replacement outages from activation decay heat and compare them with fixed ones
  waste        Waste classification (10 CFR 61.55), IAEA clearance index and recycling index of activated components
  materials    The cited materials and limits database: compositions, impurity limits, damage and gas limits
  evidence     Package and execute identified simulation evidence with real Avila Core
  design       Write and check the design file that says what a STEP model's solids are
  diff         Compare two .faris studies, or two scenario, physics, assumptions or design files: every changed parameter with old and new value and unit, causes apart from effects, and which results the change invalidates. Exits 0 when identical, 6 when they differ
  geometry     Tables about a model's geometry
  cache        Look at, check and trim the result cache
  config       Show and change your settings, and which layer supplies each value
  validate     Validate a scenario without running physics
  export       Export geometry metadata (--scenario), or a study's PDF brief, CSV and charts (--study)
  doctor       Inspect optional tool availability and file hashes without executing tools
  adapters     List the external tools FARIS can drive with version, hash and health
  control      Execute independently specified mathematical controls through the job runner
  transport    Check and normalize raw fixed-source transport artifacts; no solver invocation
  study        Generate and semantically compile a declared Core study; no solver runs
  study-file   Create, inspect, verify and unpack .faris study files
  reactor      Execute a fixed-source cold-data numerical reference through OpenMC
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version

Exit codes:
   0  ok
   1  rejected evidence: a file failed verification or compilation
   2  validation: an input is missing, unreadable or invalid
   3  solver failure: an external tool ran and did not succeed
   4  cancelled: the job was stopped by Ctrl-C or SIGTERM
   5  resource refused: the memory check refused the job
   6  different: a comparison found the two sides differ
  64  usage: the command line did not parse
```

## faris history

```text
Calculate or validate the shared Rust operating-history ledger

Usage: faris history [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run           
  validate      
  from-run      Bind rates from a revalidated successful fixed-source run and calculate history
  ensemble      Ensemble of histories on transport rates sampled from their recorded covariance; carries transport Monte Carlo uncertainty only
  compare-runs  
  sensitivity   
  help          Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris history ensemble`

## faris history ensemble

```text
Ensemble of histories on transport rates sampled from their recorded covariance; carries transport Monte Carlo uncertainty only

Usage: faris history ensemble [OPTIONS] --assumptions <ASSUMPTIONS> --rates <RATES> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --assumptions <ASSUMPTIONS>  
      --rates <RATES>              
      --samples <SAMPLES>          Number of sampled histories (1 to 2000) [default: 200]

      --units <SYSTEM>             Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

Example: `faris history ensemble`

## faris activation

```text
Activation inventory, decay heat and decay-photon source of zones through ACTINV

Usage: faris activation [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run   Run ACTINV on zones with group fluxes and an irradiation schedule; writes a JSON result with inventory, activity, decay heat, decay-photon source, pathways and data gaps
  help  Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris activation run --zones zones.json --spectra spectra.json --schedule schedule.json --cooling 1s,1h,1d,1y,10y,100y --actinv ~/.local/bin/actinv --data-dir ~/actinv-data --output activation.json`

## faris activation run

```text
Run ACTINV on zones with group fluxes and an irradiation schedule; writes a JSON result with inventory, activity, decay heat, decay-photon source, pathways and data gaps

Usage: faris activation run [OPTIONS] --actinv <ACTINV> --data-dir <DATA_DIR> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --request <REQUEST>
          A complete request (faris-activation-request/v0.1: zones with spectra, steps, cooling grid). Or give --zones, --spectra and --schedule instead
      --zones <ZONES>
          JSON list of zones: id, component_id, mass_g, volume_m3, basis, composition
      --spectra <SPECTRA>
          Normalized neutron spectra of the transport run (a list, or an object with `normalized_spectra`), 709 groups, n per m2 per s
      --schedule <SCHEDULE>
          An irradiation schedule file (faris-irradiation-schedule/v0.1)
      --cooling <COOLING>
          Cooling times since shutdown, `1s,1h,1d,1y`; 1 s to 1e9 s [default: one per decade]
      --photon-groups <PHOTON_GROUPS>
          Number of decay-photon groups (log-spaced to 20 MeV); default is ACTINV's 24 groups
      --photon-response <PHOTON_RESPONSE>
          An actinv-photon-response-1 file, for the contact dose proxy; needs its SHA-256
      --photon-response-sha256 <PHOTON_RESPONSE_SHA256>
          
      --mode <MODE>
          ACTINV solution mode. `trace` (and `auto` when it picks trace) holds the starting material constant; use `coupled` when the material itself contains radionuclides [possible values: auto, trace, coupled]
      --actinv <ACTINV>
          The `actinv` executable
      --data-dir <DATA_DIR>
          ACTINV data root (the folder above the catalogue version)
      --output <OUTPUT>
          New result file (faris-activation-result/v0.1); existing paths are refused
      --cache <CACHE>
          Content-addressed zone results; an identical request is not run again
      --work-dir <WORK_DIR>
          Scratch folder for ACTINV problems [default: OUTPUT.work]
      --top-nuclides <TOP_NUCLIDES>
          Keep this many nuclides per cooling point, most active first (totals stay complete) [default: 50]
      --photon-source-dir <PHOTON_SOURCE_DIR>
          Also write the decay-photon source (photons/s/cm3) of every zone and cooling time here
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>
          Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>
          Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

Example: `faris activation run --zones zones.json --spectra spectra.json --schedule schedule.json --cooling 1s,1h,1d,1y,10y,100y --actinv ~/.local/bin/actinv --data-dir ~/actinv-data --output activation.json`

## faris maintenance

```text
Compute replacement outages from activation decay heat and compare them with fixed ones

Usage: faris maintenance [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  run     Compute replacement outages from the decay heat of the components around the replaced part, for every design, and compare them with the fixed durations. Runs ACTINV
  report  Print a maintenance result: downtime, availability and electricity under both models, every replacement with its governing component, and the differences between designs
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris maintenance run`

## faris maintenance run

```text
Compute replacement outages from the decay heat of the components around the replaced part, for every design, and compare them with the fixed durations. Runs ACTINV

Usage: faris maintenance run [OPTIONS] --designs <DESIGNS> --assumptions <ASSUMPTIONS> --actinv <ACTINV> --data-dir <DATA_DIR> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --designs <DESIGNS>          faris-maintenance-designs/v0.1: per design the scenario, physics file, history run, 709-group spectrum run and operating-history assumptions (paths relative to the file)
      --assumptions <ASSUMPTIONS>  faris-maintenance-assumptions/v0.1: classes, thresholds, cooling grid, iteration limits
      --actinv <ACTINV>            The `actinv` executable
      --data-dir <DATA_DIR>        ACTINV data root (the folder above the catalogue version)
      --output <OUTPUT>            New result file (faris-maintenance-result/v0.1); existing paths are refused
      --cache <CACHE>              Content-addressed ACTINV points cache, shared with the Python driver [default: DECAY-CACHE inside the work folder]
      --work-dir <WORK_DIR>        Per-design, per-iteration spec folders and scratch space [default: OUTPUT.work]
      --workers <WORKERS>          Concurrent ACTINV runs [default: 1]
      --impurities <IMPURITIES>    Impurity specification (material -> impurities): use the specification-maximum variant instead of the bare lower bound
      --python <PYTHON>            Interpreter that runs the activation-input builder [default: python3]
      --builder <BUILDER>          The activation-input builder script [default: tools/build_activation_inputs.py beside the folder that holds this program (a downloaded package); otherwise the script in the source repository this program was built from]
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>        Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>             Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

Example: `faris maintenance run`

## faris waste

```text
Waste classification (10 CFR 61.55), IAEA clearance index and recycling index of activated components

Usage: faris waste [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  schemes         List the classification schemes with name, version and date, and which are implemented
  tables          Print the encoded limit tables with their source, retrieval date and licence
  classify        Classify an inventory at a disposal time. Refuses (NOT_EVALUATED) when a needed nuclide, volume, mass or flag is missing; it never defaults to Class A
  clearance-time  Find the time the IAEA clearance index falls below 1, searched between two times
  recycling       Recycling index: a dose rate over a dose-rate criterion you write. FARIS supplies no criterion
  help            Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris waste classify`


## faris waste recycling

```text
Recycling index: a dose rate over a dose-rate criterion you write. FARIS supplies no criterion

Usage: faris waste recycling [OPTIONS] --criterion <CRITERION> --contributions <CONTRIBUTIONS> --time-years <TIME_YEARS>

Options:
      --criterion <CRITERION>
          JSON with name, dose_rate_limit_sv_per_h and source
      --contributions <CONTRIBUTIONS>
          JSON list of per-nuclide dose rates with half-life and sigma

          Years after the reference at which the contributions are given [default: 0]
      --time-years <TIME_YEARS>

      --units <SYSTEM>
          Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

Example: `faris waste recycling --criterion <criterion.json> --contributions <contributions.json> --time-years 50`

## faris materials

```text
The cited materials and limits database: compositions, impurity limits, damage and gas limits

Usage: faris materials [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list           Database id, version, date and content hash; the materials and counts
  show           One material: composition, impurity specifications, properties, limits
  limits         The limit table (every row with convention, window, spectrum, conditions, status and citation)
  watchlist      The impurity watch-list with the 10 CFR 61.55 thresholds each element endangers
  check          Validate the embedded database, or another database file (schema, citations, labels)
  compare        Compare one value with one stored limit under the case's conditions
  time-to-limit  Years to each limit at a constant rate, and which is reached first. A dpa-only check is refused for a material with a helium or hydrogen limit
  classify       A waste class for a component of a stored material, only with an impurity specification
  max-impurity   The largest content of one element that keeps the inventory within a target class
  export         Export the database or its tables with citations
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris materials list`

## faris materials compare

```text
Compare one value with one stored limit under the case's conditions

Usage: faris materials compare [OPTIONS] --limit <LIMIT> --value <VALUE>

Options:
      --limit <LIMIT>             
      --value <VALUE>             
      --conditions <CONDITIONS>   JSON: dpa_convention, irradiation_temperature_c, spectrum, form (each optional)
      --override <OVERRIDE_FILE>  JSON authored override: limit_id, value, convention, author, time, reason
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>       Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>            Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
```

## faris design

```text
Write and check the design file that says what a STEP model's solids are

Usage: faris design [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  init       Read a STEP file and write a draft design file with every solid listed and every material and role left null for you to fill in
  check      Run import checks 1 to 9 on a design file and print what passed and what did not. Exit 0: no check failed. Exit 1: a check failed. Exit 2: usage or I/O error
  transport  Compute the neutron flux in the solids a fluence limit of the design applies to (the TF magnets, above 0.1 MeV, when it has none), for a design that passed `design check`, running until the mean over those solids reaches the target error. Exit 0: target reached. Exit 1: a limit stopped the run first. Exit 2: usage or I/O error
  help       Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris design init STEP`

## faris design init

```text
Read a STEP file and write a draft design file with every solid listed and every material and role left null for you to fill in

Usage: faris design init [OPTIONS] <STEP>

Arguments:
  <STEP>  

Options:
      --out <OUT>                  Where to write the draft [default: beside the STEP file]. Never overwrites
      --length-unit <LENGTH_UNIT>  The unit of a STEP file that declares none [possible values: m, cm, mm]
      --cad-python <PYTHON>        Python with cadquery, used to read the STEP file [env: FARIS_CAD_PYTHON]
      --openmc-python <PYTHON>     Python with openmc and h5py, used for the nuclear-data audit [env: FARIS_OPENMC_PYTHON]
      --cross-sections <XML>       cross_sections.xml of the audited library [env: FARIS_CROSS_SECTIONS]
      --plasma-source-path <DIR>   Directory holding the openmc_plasma_source package, for the source sites of check 9 [env: FARIS_PLASMA_SOURCE_PATH]
      --cad-reader <READER>        Which reader runs the STEP inspect and the per-solid tessellation: `native` (the OpenCASCADE worker), `python` (the helper), or `auto`, the worker when one is found and answers and the helper otherwise [default: auto; env: FARIS_CAD_READER] [possible values: auto, native, python]
      --occt-worker <WORKER>       The native CAD worker, faris-occt-worker [default: the one next to the faris program; env: FARIS_OCCT_WORKER]
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>        Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>             Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                       Print help
```

Example: `faris design init STEP`

## faris design check

```text
Run import checks 1 to 9 on a design file and print what passed and what did not. Exit 0: no check failed. Exit 1: a check failed. Exit 2: usage or I/O error

Usage: faris design check [OPTIONS] <DESIGN>

Arguments:
  <DESIGN>  

Options:
      --report <REPORT>
          Also write the report as JSON to this new file
      --work-dir <DIR>
          Keep the conversion, the per-solid tessellation, the boolean verdicts and the other products here, and reuse what is found here when its recorded STEP hash, tolerances and helper version match [default: a temporary directory, removed afterwards]
      --no-reuse
          Do everything again even when the work directory holds matching products
      --threads <N>
          Worker threads for the integrity checks [default: the available cores, at most 16]
      --seed <SEED>
          Seed of the sampling and ray directions; the same seed gives the same report [default: 1]
      --samples <SAMPLES>
          Points sampled in the bounding box (GEO-024) [default: 1000000]
      --chords <CHORDS>
          Random chords for the ray consistency check (GEO-025) [default: 100000]
      --source-sites <SOURCE_SITES>
          Source sites sampled from the plasma block (check 9) [default: 100000]
      --deviation-points <DEVIATION_POINTS>
          Points per solid the faceting deviation (GEO-032) lets OpenCASCADE project. Faces on a plane, cylinder, cone, sphere or torus are measured in closed form at every point; the points on other surfaces take an even stride of at most this many [0: all of them]. The report says which solids were sampled [default: 2000]
      --imprint-threads <IMPRINT_THREADS>
          Threads the converter may use to imprint [default: 4]
      --cad-python <PYTHON>
          Python with cadquery, used to read the STEP file [env: FARIS_CAD_PYTHON]
      --openmc-python <PYTHON>
          Python with openmc and h5py, used for the nuclear-data audit [env: FARIS_OPENMC_PYTHON]
      --cross-sections <XML>
          cross_sections.xml of the audited library [env: FARIS_CROSS_SECTIONS]
      --plasma-source-path <DIR>
          Directory holding the openmc_plasma_source package, for the source sites of check 9 [env: FARIS_PLASMA_SOURCE_PATH]
      --cad-reader <READER>
          Which reader runs the STEP inspect and the per-solid tessellation: `native` (the OpenCASCADE worker), `python` (the helper), or `auto`, the worker when one is found and answers and the helper otherwise [default: auto; env: FARIS_CAD_READER] [possible values: auto, native, python]
      --occt-worker <WORKER>
          The native CAD worker, faris-occt-worker [default: the one next to the faris program; env: FARIS_OCCT_WORKER]
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>
          Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>
          Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

Example: `faris design check`

## faris design transport

```text
Compute the neutron flux in the solids a fluence limit of the design applies to (the TF magnets, above 0.1 MeV, when it has none), for a design that passed `design check`, running until the mean over those solids reaches the target error. Exit 0: target reached. Exit 1: a limit stopped the run first. Exit 2: usage or I/O error

Usage: faris design transport [OPTIONS] --check-report <JSON> --out <DIR> <DESIGN>

Arguments:
  <DESIGN>  

Options:
      --check-report <JSON>            The report `design check --report` wrote for this design; its work directory must still hold the conversion
      --out <DIR>                      A new directory for the run. Never overwrites
      --report <REPORT>                Also write the result as JSON to this new file
      --target-error <TARGET_ERROR>    Relative standard error of the mean flux at which the run stops [default: 0.05]
      --max-histories <MAX_HISTORIES>  Stop after this many histories even when the target is not reached [default: 50000000]
      --max-seconds <MAX_SECONDS>      Stop after this many seconds of sampling even when the target is not reached [default: 3600]
      --particles <PARTICLES>          Histories per batch; the error is checked after every batch [default: 20000]
      --seed <SEED>                    [default: 1]
      --threads <THREADS>              [default: 4]
      --window-python <PYTHON>         A Python with OpenMC 0.16 or later. With it, weight windows are made for the magnets before the run, which then needs far fewer histories
      --openmc-package-path <DIR>      A directory holding an `openmc` package to use in place of --openmc-python's own, such as a build with the aiming patch
      --group <ID>                     The replacement group whose fluence limit names the solids and the energy threshold to score [default: the only group with a fluence limit]
      --cache-dir <DIR>                Where weight windows and the channel search are kept, so that a later run on the same model starts sampling at once [default: `faris-transport-cache` beside the design file]
      --no-cache                       Keep nothing between runs and reuse nothing
      --cad-python <PYTHON>            Python with cadquery, used to read the STEP file [env: FARIS_CAD_PYTHON]
      --openmc-python <PYTHON>         Python with openmc and h5py, used for the nuclear-data audit [env: FARIS_OPENMC_PYTHON]
      --cross-sections <XML>           cross_sections.xml of the audited library [env: FARIS_CROSS_SECTIONS]
      --plasma-source-path <DIR>       Directory holding the openmc_plasma_source package, for the source sites of check 9 [env: FARIS_PLASMA_SOURCE_PATH]
      --cad-reader <READER>            Which reader runs the STEP inspect and the per-solid tessellation: `native` (the OpenCASCADE worker), `python` (the helper), or `auto`, the worker when one is found and answers and the helper otherwise [default: auto; env: FARIS_CAD_READER] [possible values: auto, native, python]
      --occt-worker <WORKER>           The native CAD worker, faris-occt-worker [default: the one next to the faris program; env: FARIS_OCCT_WORKER]
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>            Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>                 Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                           Print help
```

Example: `faris design transport`

## faris cache

```text
Look at, check and trim the result cache

Usage: faris cache [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  list     List the entries: kind, key, size, when made, when last used
  verify   Rehash every entry. A damaged entry is reported and the command exits with status 1
  explain  Show every component of one entry's key, with its value
  stats    Show hit and false-hit counts, and the two rates, separately
  gc       Remove the least recently used entries until the cache is at most this size. Pinned entries are never removed
  pin      Keep an entry through `gc` and the size limit
  unpin    Let an entry be removed again
  clear    Remove every entry (and folders made before entries recorded their key)
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --dir <DIR>            The cache folder [default: `faris-transport-cache` in the current folder]
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris cache list`

```text
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

## faris study-file create

```text
Write a .faris study file from recorded transport bundles and assumptions

Usage: faris study-file create [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
  -o, --output <OUTPUT>
          New study file; an existing file is never overwritten
      --scenario <SCENARIO>
          Scenario of the port arrangement (each bundle also carries its own copy)
      --physics <PHYSICS>
          Physics input of the port arrangement; repeatable
      --bundle <BUNDLE>
          Recorded-transport bundle of the port arrangement; repeatable
      --control-scenario <CONTROL_SCENARIO>
          
      --control-physics <CONTROL_PHYSICS>
          
      --control-bundle <CONTROL_BUNDLE>
          
      --assumptions <ASSUMPTIONS>
          Operating assumptions file
      --sweep-bundle <SWEEP_BUNDLE>
          Recorded-transport bundle of the allocation sweep; repeatable
      --evidence <EVIDENCE>
          Saved-study descriptor naming Core case and workspace archives (`faris-saved-study-archive/v0.1`) or two trees of an evidence store (`faris-saved-study-store/v0.1`); repeatable, one kind per file
      --pack-evidence
          Store the Core evidence inside the file (default: by reference)
      --view <VIEW>
          JSON file with the view to record (any of: step, preset, what_if, year, field_view, history_tab, arrangement, allocation, sweep_blanket_m)
      --zstd-level <ZSTD_LEVEL>
          zstd level for recorded text [default: 15]
      --preview <PREVIEW>
          PNG thumbnail of the 3D view (at most 512 pixels a side, 512 KiB); one that does not fit is left out and reported as `preview_bytes: null`
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>
          Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>
          Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

Example: `faris study-file create --bundle port/bundles/reference.transport-bundle.json --control-bundle control/bundles/reference.transport-bundle.json --sweep-bundle sweep/blanket-045cm.transport-bundle.json --assumptions operating-assumptions.json --evidence saved-study-port-reference.json [--pack-evidence] -o demo.faris`

## faris reactor run

```text
Run one bounded fixed-source Monte Carlo calculation and retain its artifacts

Usage: faris reactor run [OPTIONS] --scenario <SCENARIO> --physics <PHYSICS> --audit <AUDIT> --cross-sections <CROSS_SECTIONS> --python <PYTHON> --openmc <OPENMC> --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --scenario <SCENARIO>
          
      --physics <PHYSICS>
          
      --audit <AUDIT>
          
      --cross-sections <CROSS_SECTIONS>
          
      --python <PYTHON>
          
      --openmc <OPENMC>
          
      --output <OUTPUT>
          New exclusive evidence directory; existing paths are refused
      --batches <BATCHES>
          Batches to run; with --target-error, the most batches (the budget) [default: 100]
      --particles <PARTICLES>
          [default: 10000]
      --seed <SEED>
          [default: 123456789]
      --threads <THREADS>
          [default: 1]
      --timeout-seconds <TIMEOUT_SECONDS>
          [default: 3600]
      --target-error <TARGET_ERROR>
          Stop once the relative standard error of the magnet fast flux reaches this (for example 0.05), after at least 30 batches, or when --batches is used up; the record states the achieved error and why it stopped
      --mesh-preset <MESH_PRESET>
          Spatial flux tally resolution; local variants use the same outboard bounds [default: coarse] [possible values: coarse, outboard-local-coarse, outboard-local, outboard-port-window]
      --activation-spectra <ACTIVATION_SPECTRA>
          Also tally each component's neutron spectrum on the 709-group `fispact-709` boundaries of the TENDL-2025 activation library (for activation inputs) [possible values: fispact-709]
      --window-python <WINDOW_PYTHON>
          A Python with OpenMC 0.16 or later. With --target-error it makes weight windows aimed at the magnet fast flux first, so the run needs far fewer histories; without it the run is analog and its record says so
      --window-cache <WINDOW_CACHE>
          Where weight windows are kept between runs [default: `faris-transport-cache` beside --output]
      --no-window-cache
          Make the weight windows for this run only
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>
          Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>
          Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help
          Print help
```

Example: `faris reactor run`

## faris reactor inspect

```text
Revalidate a saved run's exact input, artifact, volumes, and normalization

Usage: faris reactor inspect [OPTIONS] --scenario <SCENARIO> --run <RUN>

Options:
      --scenario <SCENARIO>  
      --run <RUN>            The run.json record inside a reactor evidence directory
      --setting <KEY=VALUE>  Set one setting for this run, over the environment and your settings file. Repeatable. `faris config list` shows the keys
      --units <SYSTEM>       Unit system for printed quantities: si (the default) or fusion (MW, keV, cm, GWd, dpa). The same as `--setting units.system=...`; stored files are never changed by it
  -h, --help                 Print help
```

Example: `faris reactor inspect`
